title: Randomized Clinical Trial of the use of Propofol as a sedative agent versus spinal analgesia with bupivacaine in External Cephalic Version (PropoSpinECV)
official: Randomized Clinical Trial of the use of Propofol as a sedative agent versus spinal analgesia with bupivacaine in External Cephalic Version (PropoSpinECV)
summary: Main objective: The main objective of the project is to compare the success rate of ECV when used Propofol as a sedative agent or spinal analgesia.

interventions.name: Bupivacaína B. Braun 5 mg/ml solución inyectable
Propofol Fresenius 10 mg/ml emulsión para inyección o perfusión

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Voluntary participation.
2. Older than 18 years
3. Non-cephalic presentation.
4. Desire to attempt a vaginal birth.
5. Normal blood count and coagulation prior to the intervention
Exclusion criteria:
1. Age under 18 years old.
2. Thrombocytopenia (<85,000 platelets).
3. Maternal spinal anomaly.
4. Intolerance or allergy to Propofol or any of its components.
5. Intolerance or allergy to bupivacaine or any of its components.
6. Contraindication for intrathecal sedation or analgesia
7. Multiple gestation.
8. Cephalic presentation.
9. Risk of fetal compromise.
10. Unexplained active bleeding.
11. Absolute contraindication for vaginal delivery (Placenta Previa)
12. 2 or more previous cesarean sections.
13. Previous myomectomy with entry into the uterine cavity.
14. Maternal fever.
